questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical diagnostic skills under production-like pressure, using standard Kubernetes tooling and production-ready safeguards.

## Key Concepts

- Memory pressure and OOMKilled events
- Requests/limits and QoS classes
- ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Canary rollouts and maxUnavailable
- LivenessProbe and readiness

## Code Example

```yaml
# ResourceQuota example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: mem-quot
spec:
  hard:
    requests.memory: 16Gi
    limits.memory: 32Gi
```

```yaml
# Deployment rolling update
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 25%
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you detect a memory leak vs transient spike?
- What metrics and alerts would you add for ongoing health?
- How would you automate this process in a future incident?

## Why This Is Asked
RBAC misconfig can leak data across namespaces. This tests ability to audit, isolate, and enforce least privilege in a real cluster.

## Key Concepts
- RBAC: Roles vs ClusterRoles
- Namespace scoping
- kubectl can-i and impersonation
- Least privilege enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# apps/roles/app-read.yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: apps
  name: app-read
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets","configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```

```yaml
# apps/roles/app-sa-binding.yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: app-read-binding
  namespace: apps
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: app-sa
  namespace: apps
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: app-read
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

## Why This Is Asked
Auditing is central to security and compliance; this tests practical setup of an external webhook sink with a canary rollout and safe rollback procedures.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Audit policy configuration
- AuditSink and webhook sink implementation
- Canary rollout strategy and rollback mechanisms
- Retry logic, exponential backoff, and rate limiting

## Code Example
```yaml
# audit-policy.yaml
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
rules:
- level: Metadata
  resources:
  - group: ""
    resources: ["pods","configmaps","secrets"]
```

```yaml
# audit-sink.yaml (canary sink)
apiVersion: auditregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: AuditSink
metadata:
  name: audit-sink-canary
spec:
  webhook:
    clientConfig:
      service:
        name: audit-webhook-service
        namespace: audit-system
        path: "/audit"
      timeout: 30s
    throttle:
      qps: 10
      burst: 20
    retryBackoff:
      base: 1s
      max: 30s
```

```bash
# Apply audit policy and canary sink
kubectl apply -f audit-policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f audit-sink-canary.yaml

# Generate test events
kubectl run test-pod --image=nginx --restart=Never
kubectl delete pod test-pod

# Verify SIEM ingestion and proceed to full rollout
curl -X POST https://siem-endpoint/audit/check
kubectl apply -f audit-sink-full.yaml
```
